To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vegetation history of the Mackenzie Mts. during the late Quaternary has been dominated by changes in treeline position, and that the timing of these changes has been consistent with the predicted response to changes in summer insolution.

the vegetation history of the Mackenzie Mountain region was characterized by the expansion of shrub tundra, the establishment of a Picea forest, the establishment of Alnus and the establishment of the current vegetation composition.

(i) Artemisia and Salx-dominated herb-tundra occupied the Mackenzie Mountains from at least 11,500 to ca. 10.200 yr B.P.; (ii) shrub tundra, dominated by Betula, expanded throughout the region ca. 10 200 yr B.P. to 8500 yr BP; (iii) Picea arrived by 8500 BP, expanded to the current treeline elevation by 8000 BP and became established in the forest

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vegetation history of the Mackenzie Mountain region is similar to the history of vegetation in the Yukon, and that the vegetation history is a response to climate change.
the vegetation of the central Mackenize Mountains has been responding to climate change for at least the past 12,000 years, with the greatest change occurring between 11,000 and 8000 yr ago.
Picea has expanded into the treeline region of the Mackenzie Mountain in response to increasing summer insolation, but has declined in density in the late Holocne.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treeline of the Mackenzie Mountain region has not been stable over time, and that the current position of the treeline is not a result of climatic conditions prevailing at the present time.
the central Mackenzie Mountain treeline is currently at its highest position since deglaciation.

Picea has been a dominant species at the current treeline for at least 8000 yr and that the present composition and structure of the forest-tundra and treeline vegetation are a result of the interaction of the present climatic conditions with a vegetation history which is dominated by Picea and which has not changed significantly in the past 8000 yr.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vegetation of this region has been in a dynamic equilibrium since at least 12 ka BP.
the vegetation history in the central Mackenize Mountains was similar to that observed elsewhere in the western Cordillera.
Picea has been present in the central Mackenize Mountains since at least 8500 yr BP, and has been a dominant species in the forest-tundras and open forests of the region for the last ∼ 6000 yr.
